syllabus_topics: The quantum revolution; Phenomenological basis of Quantum Mechanics; Wave-particle duality
Superposition principle; wave function and probabilistic interpretation
One-dimensional potentials. Bound and scattering states; Tunneling effect; harmonic oscillator; applications
The 3-dimensional Schrodinger equation; the Hydrogen atom
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) for the course is calculated as NF=max(0.5*NE+0.5*NQ,NE), where NE is the exam grade and NQ is the average quiz grade. The quizzes are not mandatory and have no minimum grade. The exam (NE) has a minimum grade of 7.5. To pass the course, NF must be greater than or equal to 9.5 and NE must be greater than or equal to 7.5.
bibliography: David Griffiths, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, 2nd Edition, Pearson International Edition, Pearson Prentice Hall, 2005 (main)
